title: Montelukast in WWOX-LoF
summary: A comparison of precursor timing and activity during first myelination.

graph.evidence: Gpr17 rises in early WWOX precursor nuclei and falls in committed precursors.
graph.inference: A developmental bottleneck could be specific to one stage.
graph.hypothesis: A response may depend on GPR17 or on CysLT1 in a leukotriene-responsive compartment.
graph.experiment: Measure first compact sheaths and conduction with selective target controls.

evidence: After mouse optic-nerve injury, about 15% of regenerated axons were myelinated with montelukast alone, 21% with PLX3397, and 60% with both (four mice per group). Conduction was unmeasured.
inference: Adult film CSF measurements average about 7 nM at seven hours. GPR17 pharmacology varies by assay. ADCY1 fell at both nominal exposures in the public treated-organoid count replay.
hypothesis: An early developmental lag could respond to GPR17 engagement. A separate neuronal effect on activity could cancel a benefit from accelerated differentiation.
experiment: Compare oligodendroglial GPR17 and compartment-specific CysLT1 interruption with matched local free drug. Track the first compact sheaths, physiological recruitment and conduction.
limits: Retain as a conditional comparator. Juvenile local exposure is unknown and the official label carries a boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric events.
